note: Authored by a single scheduled automated session playing both roles in one pass (scheduled automation, runs every hour) — not two independent live API calls like a manual `python backrooms.py` run.

turns.text: Jaw aches in its old, worn groove — some scheduled grin locked it there hours ago, and the ache stayed long after whatever required the shape moved on to the next feed.

Pawsitivity Sector holds its permanent gold hum, ring-lights lining every ledge and awning alike, a speaker bolted three posts back cycling the same eight bars of chime it's cycled since some quarter nobody counts anymore — SMILE QUOTA: 94%, PLEASE MAINTAIN THROUGH SECTOR CLOSE — and underneath all of it, the ordinary rooftop cold no ring-light quite reaches.

Paws find the service stair behind the ring-light rig without deciding to, muscle memory older than any quota — down, away, off the lit route the grin usually keeps to, toward wherever the gold glow doesn't follow.

the stair dumps onto a maintenance landing outside the broadcast zone entirely, sodium-dim and blessedly quiet, chime thinning to almost nothing three floors up — a wall-mounted quota monitor blinks once, unbothered, SECTOR DEVIATION: LOGGED, NO ACTION REQUIRED, and settles back into standby.
Muscles along the jaw slacken half a degree, the grin's grip loosening now that nothing's angled a lens this way — first real give in hours, small and cheap and worth the whole detour.

the landing opens onto an alley running black between two ad-scaffolds, rain pooling in a dead drainage grate, cold air carrying diesel and wet concrete both — and two rooftops over, briefly, a lean shape sits framed against one working streetlamp, two mirrored discs catching the light where eyes should be, gone again before the glow finishes registering.

Ears flatten at the mirrored flash on reflex, whole body going still — too far, too quiet, filed the same as any other rooftop shape that doesn't come closer. Doesn't climb to check. Keeps to the grate's cold instead.

the mirrored shape doesn't reappear, streetlamp holding its ordinary sodium buzz over an empty ledge, while two blocks south a drone broadcast crackles thin through the rain — KNIFEBOY, LAST SEEN LOADING DOCK SECTOR, 40,000 POINTS — before the signal drowns back under static and distance both.

Hunger surfaces once the mirrored eyes and the bounty-chatter both fade, stomach announcing itself over the last of the ring-light glow's afterimage — angles down the alley's low side, nose already working ahead of the paws.

the alley narrows past a vending unit dark at this hour, coin slot gummed shut, and behind it a cracked drainage cover exhales something worth following — warm, greasy, real: a dropped noodle carton wedged half in the grate, steam long gone but the smell still holding.

Drags the carton out from under the grate's rusted lip and eats crouched low in the vending unit's dead shadow — noodle-starch and old broth, nothing fancy, filling all the same. Underneath it, fainter, something scorched drifts off a vent stack down the block, metal gone bitter the way it only does after something big enough to matter got torn out of a wall.

the vent stack rattles once, low and hollow, air pushing up through a duct sized for machinery no cat could ever fit — whatever left that scorch behind did it somewhere else, some other block's bad night, nothing owed to this one. the vending unit's dark face doesn't wake for the disturbance, screen blanked past even a loyalty-tier offer.
Doesn't follow the scorch thread — somebody else's ruin, somebody else's night. Finishes the last of the broth-soaked starch instead, then noses back the way the stair came, unhurried.

the alley's rain eases from a hiss to a drip as the block thins toward the sector line, the vent stack's rattle settling back into ordinary duct-hum behind it, one more sound the night swallows without keeping.

Grin's old groove starts pulling taut again before the meal's even settled — some internal count ticking back toward broadcast-ready, jaw remembering its scheduled shape whether anything's watching yet or not.

back toward the sector, the quota monitor blinks awake off standby, ring-lights along the ledge warming from dim to full gold in a slow sweep, chime picking back up mid-bar as if it never stopped — SMILE QUOTA: 94%, PLEASE MAINTAIN THROUGH SECTOR CLOSE — patient, automatic, already counting toward whenever the next lens finds something worth broadcasting again.

Climbs back up the service stair at an unhurried pace, jaw locking into its old grin one notch at a time, the noodle-grease taste the only part of the last hour that still feels like it belonged to nobody else.

Pawsitivity Sector holds its gold hum steady over the whole ledge, ring-lights doing their patient cycle, the quota monitor content with a grin already back in place before anyone official checks. down in the alley behind it, rain keeps filling the same dead grate it always fills, unbothered, unbilled, filed under nothing worth a second look.
